title: Exploration of Potential Molecular Mechanisms and Key Genes Related to T-Cell Exhaustion in Coronary Heart Disease from a Bioinformatics Perspective.
authors: Liu, Fei; Liu, Wen; Zhang, Zhiliang; Peng, Xiaoping; Wen, Yuan
journal: Critical reviews in eukaryotic gene expression
one_liner_zh: 该文从生物信息学角度探索冠心病中T细胞耗竭相关关键基因，虽涉及转录因子调控网络和分子对接，但核心对象非蛋白质-DNA互作，且方法以常规组学统计为主，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Coronary heart disease (CHD), a major cardiovascular disorder, is associated with T cell exhaustion (TEX) in its pathogenesis. This study aimed to identify TEX-related key genes in CHD and explore their potential mechanisms. The training set, validation set, and TEX-related genes (TEX-RGs) were downloaded from public databases. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified and intersected with TEX-RGs to obtain candidate genes. LASSO regression and Wilcoxon rank-sum test were then used to screen key genes. A nomogram for CHD prediction was constructed and validated via calibration curves and ROC curves. Finally, analyses related to functional enrichment, cell infiltration, T cell state score (TCSS) evaluation, regulatory network construction, drug prediction, and molecular docking were performed for key genes. Initially, the 48 candidate genes were identified, followed by the determination of two key genes (BST2 and XPC). A nomogram integrating BST2 and XPC showed high prediction performance. Functional enrichment analysis indicated their involvement in oxidative phosphorylation, spliceosome, and other processes. Notably, CHD patients exhibited altered infiltration of CD8+ effector memory T cells and chondrocytes, with imbalanced TCSS in Quiescence and Terminal Exhaustion T cell subsets. Regulatory network analysis identified transcription factors (e.g., GATA1, and SP1), microRNAs (e.g., hsa-miR-942-5p), and long non-coding RNAs (e.g., H19) associated with key genes. Potential drugs interacting with key genes (e.g., alvespimycin, MG-262) were predicted, though molecular docking revealed weak binding ability. Collectively, these findings provided valuable insights into the molecular mechanisms of CHD, offering a theoretical basis for understanding the disease and developing targeted therapeutic strategies.
abstract_zh: 冠心病（CHD）作为一种主要的心血管疾病，其发病机制与T细胞耗竭（TEX）相关。本研究旨在识别CHD中与TEX相关的关键基因，并探讨其潜在机制。训练集、验证集及TEX相关基因（TEX-RGs）均从公共数据库下载。鉴定差异表达基因（DEGs）并与TEX-RGs取交集以获得候选基因。随后，使用LASSO回归和Wilcoxon秩和检验筛选关键基因。构建用于CHD预测的列线图，并通过校准曲线和ROC曲线进行验证。最后，对关键基因进行了功能富集、细胞浸润、T细胞状态评分（TCSS）评估、调控网络构建、药物预测及分子对接等相关分析。初步鉴定出48个候选基因，随后确定两个关键基因（BST2和XPC）。整合BST2和XPC的列线图显示出较高的预测性能。功能富集分析表明它们参与氧化磷酸化、剪接体等过程。值得注意的是，CHD患者表现出CD8+效应记忆T细胞和软骨细胞浸润的改变，且在静止和终末耗竭T细胞亚群中TCSS失衡。调控网络分析鉴定了与关键基因相关的转录因子（如GATA1、SP1）、微小RNA（如hsa-miR-942-5p）和长链非编码RNA（如H19）。预测了与关键基因相互作用的潜在药物（如alvespimycin、MG-262），但分子对接显示结合能力较弱。总体而言，这些发现为CHD的分子机制提供了有价值的见解，为理解该疾病和制定靶向治疗策略提供了理论基础。
